items.title: Hackers abused GL.iNet's cloud service to plant malware on routers and KVM devices
items.why: GL.iNet says attackers used a flaw in its GoodCloud remote management service to install malware on routers and remote KVM devices. The cloud hole is closed, but already-infected devices still carry the malware.
items.action: Update every GL.iNet router and KVM to the newest firmware, and if one shows signs of infection, reinstall firmware without saved settings and change its passwords.

items.title: Cleverbridge says hackers copied card numbers and CVVs from its software checkout platform
items.why: Cleverbridge, which handles online checkout for many software and SaaS vendors, says a third party copied stored card numbers, expiry dates and security codes. It began notifying customers on Nov. 20 and has not said how many were affected.
items.action: Check recent card statements for any software you bought online, and ask your bank to reissue a card if you get a Cleverbridge notice.

items.title: Palo Alto firewalls with HTTP/2 turned on need fixes for two critical NGINX flaws
items.why: Palo Alto Networks says two critical NGINX flaws reach PAN-OS and Panorama when HTTP/2 is enabled, with no login needed. It knows of no attacks yet, and some fixed builds are due around Nov. 23.
items.action: Install the fixed PAN-OS build for your version, or turn off HTTP/2 on PAN-OS and Panorama until you can.

items.title: Info-stealing malware on 600 PCs harvested US bank, Login.gov and Microsoft 365 access
items.why: Researchers at Hunt.io found the stash of a credential-theft operation that infected 603 Windows PCs since October, taking bank and government logins, a password vault and Microsoft 365 session cookies that skipped MFA.
items.action: Require phishing-resistant MFA and device-based conditional access for Microsoft 365, and reset passwords and sessions on any PC you suspect is infected.

items.title: Attackers used an AI agent tool to find an unknown flaw and take over a server in minutes
items.why: Amazon says a likely China-linked group used the open-source AI framework Cairn to find a zero-day in a medical imaging app and gain root access, moving from mapping to exploit in about 11 minutes.
items.action: Patch internet-facing apps quickly and remove or lock down any exposed admin or testing panels, since automated tools now find them fast.

items.title: WhatsApp fixes a bug scammers used to make their messages look more legitimate
items.why: WhatsApp's November advisory fixes three flaws, including one in Click to WhatsApp ads that a scammer exploited in a live campaign. WhatsApp Business on Android is among the affected apps.
items.action: Update WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business on every company and personal phone used for customer contact.
